note: Decision queue: 'Current' describes the live setting; recommendations are proposals, not owner approvals. Optional changes remain unimplemented until chosen. The G-02 purchase-link hold is a safety gate and cannot be bypassed without recorded validation. Reply with a suggestion ID and option letter (for example 'S-03 B').

options.label: Keep the earlier /editorial/ edition live but excluded from search, and index only the root site (current).
options.tradeoff: Nothing is lost and there is one indexed site; the old edition is still public if someone has the URL.

options.label: Retire /editorial/ entirely and redirect its URLs to the equivalent root pages.
options.tradeoff: Cleanest signal for search engines; a redirect map has to be written and tested first.

options.label: Merge the better parts of the old edition into the root site and remove the duplicate pages.
options.tradeoff: Best content outcome, most work, and the old edition's data conflicts with the root data and must be reconciled.

suggestions.recommendation: B once the redirect map is written. Two editions of a five-page site is more surface than the content justifies.

suggestions.topic: Buy buttons while links are untested

options.label: Keep buy buttons while the Associates test is pending (not selected).
options.tradeoff: The site can earn from day one, but an untested link that silently fails credits nothing.

options.label: Hide every buy button until gate G-02 passes (current).
options.tradeoff: Maximum compliance confidence; the site earns nothing until the owner tests.

suggestions.recommendation: B until every product has a recorded Associates Central test, confirmed destination, and tracking-report evidence.

options.label: Run tools/collector.mjs on a small VPS the owner controls, behind HTTPS.
options.tradeoff: Full control of raw data; the owner runs a server and patches it.

options.label: Run it as a serverless function on a platform that supports Node.
options.tradeoff: No server to patch; cold starts and platform limits on storage.

options.label: Skip self-hosting and use a privacy-focused hosted analytics service.
options.tradeoff: Fastest to start; one more third party, and the data leaves your control.

options.label: Stay inactive until there is traffic worth measuring (current).
options.tradeoff: Zero maintenance; decisions stay on instinct, which is exactly what the brief asks to avoid.

suggestions.recommendation: B. It removes the server maintenance objection without handing the data away.

options.label: Show no prices; every button reads 'Check the current price on Amazon' (current).
options.tradeoff: Always accurate, and compliant with the price clause; readers have to click to know a budget.

options.label: Enroll in the Creators API and display Amazon-served prices with a timestamp.
options.tradeoff: Better for budget-led shoppers; more engineering, and a stale price is a compliance risk.

options.label: Show a coarse price band instead of a figure.
options.tradeoff: Useful and stable; still a claim that needs checking, and it ages badly.

suggestions.recommendation: A until traffic justifies the Creators API work. Then B.

options.label: One new guide every two weeks (current).
options.tradeoff: Sustainable; slow to build a topic cluster.

options.label: One new guide per week.
options.tradeoff: Faster topical coverage; needs a real writing slot weekly.

options.label: A batch of eight guides before launch, then monthly.
options.tradeoff: Reaches a useful site size quickly; risks thin pages if the batch is rushed.

suggestions.recommendation: A, at a quality bar high enough that every guide earns its place. Ten thin guides are worse than four good ones.

options.label: No email capture yet; the RSS feed is the only subscription route (current).
options.tradeoff: Nothing to maintain and no consent obligations; no direct channel to readers.

options.label: Add a single-field email capture with double opt-in on guide pages.
options.tradeoff: Owns the audience instead of renting it from search; adds a privacy notice and a provider.

options.label: Publish a 'notify me when a new guide ships' link that opens a mail draft.
options.tradeoff: Zero infrastructure and honest; very low conversion.

suggestions.recommendation: B only once there are at least three guides worth returning for. Before that it is asking for an email with nothing to send.

options.label: Keep editorial illustration, clearly labelled as not the reviewed unit (current).
options.tradeoff: Consistent look, no licensing exposure, no misleading product photography.

options.label: Use Amazon-hosted product images through the approved image service.
options.tradeoff: Shows the actual product; images must be served by Amazon's tools and can change without notice.

options.label: Commission real photography of the units.
options.tradeoff: Highest trust and highest cost; needs physical units.

suggestions.recommendation: B for the product hero on each product page, A everywhere else. Readers want to see the actual thing they are buying.

options.label: Keep the team byline, flagged as a weakness (current).
options.tradeoff: Honest and unchanging; weaker trust signal than a person.

options.label: Add a named editor with a short bio and a contact address.
options.tradeoff: Strongest trust signal; a person has to be accountable for the corrections.

suggestions.recommendation: B as soon as a real person will take the byline. This is one of the cheapest trust wins available.

options.label: Stay at five submitted products and go deep on them (current).
options.tradeoff: Focused and honest; a thin catalogue for a shopping site.

options.label: Add three to five comparison products per category, researched the same way.
options.tradeoff: Makes the categories credible; each added product needs its own source page and verification.

options.label: Expand into a second niche once the first converts.
options.tradeoff: Scales the model; splits attention before anything is proven.

suggestions.recommendation: B, one category at a time, and only where a manufacturer page exists to verify against.

options.label: Dark disclosure bar directly under the masthead, repeated in the footer (current).
options.tradeoff: Impossible to miss, and slightly heavy visually.

options.label: A lighter inline notice above the first product, plus the footer repeat.
options.tradeoff: Prettier; risks being read as decoration rather than disclosure.

suggestions.recommendation: A. The FTC standard is that the disclosure must be hard to miss, and this one is.

options.label: Keep research and publishing manual for now; use explicit source, validation, and disclosure gates (current).
options.tradeoff: No provider cost or generated claims, but no automated research or drafts.

options.label: Pilot AI-assisted drafts using only approved product/query data, with citations and mandatory human approval.
options.tradeoff: Can speed research and first drafts; requires an authorized source, model/provider, data terms, budget, and named editor.

options.label: Automatically publish AI-generated product pages and links.
options.tradeoff: Highest automation and risk; requires validated source data, policy checks, working analytics, and rollback owner. Not recommended now.

suggestions.recommendation: B only after Q-14 and D-09 are answered; do not automate publication before evidence and review gates exist.
